memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'They are to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the food offerings presented to the LORD. It is a sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for them for any of these sins they have committed, and they will be forgiven. The rest of the offering will belong to the priest, as in the grain offering.'" - Lev 5:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A handful of flour, burned on top of offerings already on the altar. And the same words follow that have followed the bull, the goat, the lamb, and the birds: they will be forgiven.

God has now said "forgiven" over the wealthiest and the poorest in Israel, in identical language. A bull and two litres of flour receive the same verdict.

If forgiveness could be bought, the price would matter. It cannot, so it does not.

This should silence forever the fear that some people are more forgivable than others. In the church we can unconsciously rank people — the respectable believer with the clean past, and the one with a history everyone knows about. God's altar does not work that way. Christ died for the ungodly (Rom 5:6), and there is no category of person He died for more.

Notice also the last line: the rest belongs to the priest. Even the poorest man's offering fed someone. His flour, small as it was, sustained a family serving in God's house.

Nothing you bring God is too small to be useful to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I secretly believe some people are harder for God to forgive than others?
2. Have I dismissed my small offering as not worth bringing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your forgiveness is not sold by weight. Receive what little I have, and use it for Your purposes. Amen.
